night.text: KOReader's night mode inverts the whole framebuffer. The plugin draws the inverse of these colours while night mode is on, so the panel shows what you see here; covers are pre-inverted too, so they stay true. Verify on the device in stage 1.

words.text: No drag on e-ink. Reordering is up and down arrows; adding is a picker; every change repaints once. Rows and launcher entries are the two hand-written menus; everything else is generated from the schema.

scale.text: Every board is the Kindle Colorsoft at half size: 632×840 here is 1264×1680 on the device. Text sizes double on the device.

looks.text: A and C share every widget and every gesture. They differ only in tokens: two type faces, five or six colours by role, stroke weight, shadow offset, corner radius, tile style. A look is a small table, not code.

gestures.text: One vocabulary everywhere. Tap acts: the cover opens the book, a launcher entry runs, weather refreshes. Hold opens the menu for what you held. Swipe down from the top edge is still KOReader's own menu.

menu.text: The settings menu is KOReader's own menu widget, generated from schema.lua. A look does not restyle it: native menus stay native, so KOReader upgrades can't break them.

pw.text: Kindle Paperwhite, 11th generation assumed: 1236×1648 at 300 DPI, 16 grey levels, so 618×824 here. Greys are chosen for e-ink contrast, not desaturated from the colour boards.
